newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Offers mostly steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Offers mostly steady to lower.

text.p: Rail and truck soymeal offers fell sharply in some southern U.S. Midwest locations as new crop supplies became more readily available, several U.S. cash soymeal brokers said.
"We were astronomically high because of the rain," a Kansas merchandiser said, referring to last week's harvest delays. "The weather is clear, the beans are coming in and our basis is dropping."
Offers dropped $4 a ton in Kansas City and $6 a ton in Minnesota as new crop supplies began filling the pipeline.
Movement was said to be slow as export demand remained stagnant.
In Indiana, harvest was progressing well but moisture levels were said to be high. Early harvested fields were producing yields in the upper 40-bushels-per-acre area to lower 50s, a dealer said.
